clue.text: Some learn of what divides houses in Italian city

definitions.text: what divides houses in Italian city

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that some people learn which street or wall separates rival families in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The houses are families, the Montagues and Capulets of the theme, and the river is a fair stand-in for anything splitting an Italian city's houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the river flowing through Florence, splitting the city's buildings between its two banks.

clue.text: Suppresses son Mike et al

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
et al, Latin 'and others', means others

explanation.surface: A complaint that a boy, Mike and the rest keep things quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to stifle or hold it down, a close synonym of suppress.

clue.text: What causes global revolution? Nothing

definitions.meaning: the saying that ... makes the world go round
a zero score in tennis is called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially it makes the world go round, and in tennis scoring it stands for zero.

clue.text: Like Valentine I put in poetic form

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the poetic form

parts.note: verse is the form of poetry
I as the Roman numeral, or the pronoun, can stand for one

explanation.surface: A remark that a love note was written in verse, like a Valentine card.
explanation.walkthrough: Valentine is not the card but the gentleman in Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona, which fits the Verona theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentine is one of the two gentlemen from Verona, so he is a native of that city.

clue.text: It enables entries with top cards, holding clubs and spades

indicators.note: holding means the top cards contain the clubs abbreviation

parts.note: aces are the highest cards in many games
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
S is the card-game abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player's hand with high cards, clubs and spades that opens the way into the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is the means of getting in, so it is what permits entry.

clue.text: Trusted friend's name appearing in end of Act I, possibly

indicators.note: appearing in puts the name abbreviation among the rearranged letters
possibly signals the letters of end of Act I can be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A trusted friend's name turns up at the close of the first act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges END OF ACT I to CONFIDATE, and 'appearing in' slots N in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidante is a woman to whom secrets are entrusted, a close and trusted friend.

clue.text: Theatrical miss with little time — she was meant to go to 26 across

definitions.text: she was meant to go to 26 across

parts.note: Miss Julie is the heroine of Strindberg's play of that name
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A stage actress is late, and she was supposed to be heading for the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is PARIS: the County Paris, whom Juliet was meant to marry, not the city it pretends to be.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy the heroine's parents arranged for her to marry the County Paris.

clue.text: Scoff at European cafe, finally, between 7 and 9

indicators.note: between puts the two E letters in the middle of the pair from 7 and 9

parts.note: the answer to 7 is the NATO alphabet word for J
the answer to 9 is the NATO alphabet word for R

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of cafe

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a European cafe that sits between two other places.
explanation.walkthrough: Answers 7 and 9 are themselves NATO alphabet words, giving J and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer at someone is to mock or deride them, the same as to scoff at them.

clue.text: Passionate fellow in back of Italian car?

definitions.meaning: a byword for an ardent male lover, after Shakespeare's hero
the second word of the Italian car make Alfa ...

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's hero is a byword for an ardent lover, and is the second half of the Alfa Romeo marque.

clue.text: Addition to letter that could come from one's cruel pen

indicators.note: that could come from signals the letters of the following words being reworked

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe is no letter, so this gives ONES
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something added to a letter written by a cruel person's pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' ends the surface and also hints at a second sense, a pen being an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure is something put into the envelope alongside a letter.

clue.text: See 13
For example, drug supplier for 7, or murder investigator in …

definitions.meaning: ... Laurence gives Juliet the potion that makes her seem dead
William of Baskerville, the monk who solves murders in Eco's novel at 13

explanation.definitionFit: Both a holy brother: Laurence who drugs Juliet, and William who investigates the abbey killings.

clue.text: … 18's work that's irrelevant when it's 17

definitions.meaning: the novel by Umberto Eco, the author at 18
Juliet says a rose by any other name would smell as sweet, so its label is irrelevant when nosed

explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of Eco's medieval mystery, and Juliet's speech says a flower's label matters nothing to its smell.

clue.text: One century after another — that's invigorating

indicators.note: after places the single-century letters behind the other century

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, another century
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Scoring one hundred runs after another is a real boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Century in cricket means a hundred runs; TON is British slang for a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic is used as an adjective meaning restorative or bracing, giving strength.

clue.text: Like some Spaniards having a change of land in USA

indicators.note: change of signals the letters of the following words being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some Spanish people moving to live in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is only a link; the A it seems to introduce is itself part of the pool, the rest rearranged by 'change of' into NDALUSIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusia is a region of southern Spain, so its people are Spaniards of that kind.

clue.text: Calms down — in past, passed a test

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the words passed a test

explanation.surface: Someone who once passed an exam is calm about it now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' points to the past-tense word passed in which the run begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate a patient is to calm them, usually with a drug.

clue.text: Part in play understood in audience

indicators.note: in audience means as heard by listeners

parts.note: seen, as in 'I see', means understood

explanation.surface: A part in a play is grasped by the audience watching it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a division of an act in a play.

clue.text: Moved cautiously to sign agreement, including opponents at table

indicators.note: including means the nod contains the pair of opponents

parts.note: to nod is to signal agreement
at bridge South and East sit as opponents

explanation.surface: A bridge player cautiously agrees a deal involving the opponents at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South partner against East and West, so S and E are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to edge ahead carefully, as a vehicle does into traffic.

clue.text: Author announced what precedes foxtrot

indicators.note: announced means as spoken aloud

parts.note: Echo comes just before Foxtrot in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer is named before the ballroom dance begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot is not the dance but F in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist, writer of The Name of the Rose.

clue.text: Zero on bungled subtest? That's extremely stupid

parts.note: O resembles the figure zero

indicators.note: bungled suggests the letters of subtest are mangled

explanation.surface: Getting nought on a botched little test is the height of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, and this superlative form means most dense.

clue.text: Fish from 6 to 7

definitions.meaning: a ... shark or nursehound is a kind of fish
the confidante to Juliet in the play is her old ...

explanation.definitionFit: A nurse shark is a fish, and Juliet's Nurse is her chief confidante in the play.

clue.text: European left-winger held up by another came back

indicators.note: held, with by, means the second left-winger encloses the others

parts.note: a red is another word for a left-winger

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, reads the left-winger from bottom to top

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: A European socialist is propped up by a comrade and returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TROT to TORT; E and TORT are 'held' by RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to answer back sharply, so this is a past-tense reply.

clue.text: Unusually apt clue for "playhouse"?

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of apt clue being arranged oddly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of an apt clue for a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playhouse' is not a theatre but a house, a family, in the play: Juliet's family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capulets are one of the two feuding houses in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Annual payment for accommodating contents of 2, perhaps

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation of per annum, yearly
rent is what one pays for housing

explanation.surface: Yearly charge for housing what is in a box, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The inside of 2's answer, minus its outer S letters, gives MOTHER, a parent; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of a parent, mother or father.

clue.text: How 9 described 7 in morning paper

definitions.meaning: Romeo says Juliet is ... in the balcony scene
a British daily tabloid newspaper of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Romeo says Juliet is the sun, and it is also the title of a British daily tabloid newspaper.

clue.text: Scene of play in which fighting takes place

definitions.meaning: a building where plays are staged

explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse where dramas are staged, and the arena of a war, as in theatre of operations.

clue.text: He won the heart of a beauty in romantic city

definitions.text: He won the heart of a beauty
definitions.meaning: the Trojan prince who carried off Helen
the French capital, known as the city of love

explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince won Helen of Troy, and the French capital is famed for romance.

clue.text: Interrogate arrogant young man about maiden

indicators.note: about means the young man surrounds the maiden

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky or conceited youth
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Questioning a cocky lad about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information.

clue.text: Facing early light daters saw spread around

indicators.note: spread around signals the letters being scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Couples on a date watched the dawn while sitting about.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn comes from the east, so heading that way means facing the sunrise.

clue.text: Sets composed in extra musical setting for tragic story

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the extra

parts.note: a wide is an extra run in cricket, from a ball bowled out of reach

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters of sets are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Stage sets are built for a musical version of a sad tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' gives ESTS. A wide is a cricket extra: a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, which adds a run to the score.
explanation.definitionFit: West Side Story is the musical that resets Romeo and Juliet in New York's Upper West Side.

clue.text: See 28
Sequences of film about upper-class family

indicators.note: about means the film sequences surround the class letter

parts.note: montages are edited sequences of film shots

explanation.surface: Film sequences are made about a posh family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Montagues are Romeo's household, one of the two feuding houses in the play.

clue.text: Expedition from way down South, heading West

indicators.note: heading west, in an across entry, means read from right to left

parts.note: deep means far down

explanation.surface: An expedition from far south heads off towards the west.
explanation.walkthrough: Expedition here is not a journey but its old sense of promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or haste, which is speed.
